messages:
alex: alerting — observability shows p95 east->west latency jump (~200ms -> 1.2s) in us-west-gpu pool starting 18:02, coincides with peak batching window. Affected ~14 nodes across two racks.
rachel: seeing same on tracing, requests hit KV cache miss then huge tail. Any packet loss metrics? :thinking:
dmitri: packet loss up on a subset of paths, small but spikes align with batch ramp. I ran a quick `mtr` between two affected nodes, intermittent 1-3% loss on hop 3.
kai: batching profile changed today? We rolled a new config that increases max_batch_tokens from 1024->2048 at 18:00 for Canary A. Could increase headroom on NVLink?
alex: correct, Canary A got heavier tails. But non-canary nodes also impacted in same racks. Could be network-level.
maria: ops-bot reported a NIC firmware push completed at 17:50 on rack-12 and rack-13. Could be a bad firmware combo with kernel tso/gso.
rachel: good call — check ethtool stats and dev drops. If TXQ/backlog or gro/gso fragmentation spikes that would blow bursts during batching.
dmitri: `ssh node-12-03 sudo ethtool -S eth0 | grep -E "tx_|rx_"` shows tx_drops climbing during the window. Also `dmesg` shows offload warnings on one host.
alex: can someone run `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/ew.pcap udp` during next window? Keep capture 2 mins.
kai: running small probe now with iperf3 across nodes to reproduce quickly. If we can reproduce with smaller payloads that's helpful.
maria: ops-bot says topology changed — ECMP rebalancer bumped routes for a subset of flows at 18:01 due to a transient link degradation in ToR-A. That might explain why only certain paths.
dmitri: ran `iperf3 -u -b 10G` between node-12-03 and node-13-07 while increasing synthetic batch requests — saw periodic latency spikes and duplicate ACKs every ~5s. That screams NIC coalescing + retransmit.
rachel: temporary mitigation: throttling batch size on Canary A to previous value and pinning traffic away from affected ToRs via placement policy. Can we roll that in now?
alex: agreed — kai, can you revert Canary A max_batch_tokens to 1024 for the rest of the peak hour? Also move incoming routing for in-flight Dedicated jobs off rack-12/13 via `placement: avoid:rack-12,rack-13` rule in the scheduler.
kai: reverting now and submitting placement change. Will monitor p95.
deploy-bot: rollout started: config revert to Canary A (max_batch_tokens=1024) on 6 pods.
ops-bot: note: firmware vendor reported a known issue with certain offload flags + kernel 5.15 causing TX queue stall under large burst. Patch ETA 48h.
dmitri: long-term fix options: 1) schedule vendor firmware reflash + kernel upgrade, 2) disable TSO/GSO on affected NICs, 3) add hw steering tweak to re-balance ECMP. Disabling TSO/GSO is lowest risk quick test.
maria: cost note — moving traffic plus throttling increases inference cost ~8% for affected customers this window. Ops will flag billing if it persists.
rachel: current p95 back down to ~260ms after revert/placement. Keeping watch for 30m.
alex: action items: dmitri validate `ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off` impact on a test node; maria coordinate vendor patch scheduling; kai complete placement rule and confirm no regressions; rachel continue monitoring + create follow-up postmortem.
maria: will open vendor ticket and cc infra-security.
dmitri: testing TSO/GSO toggle now on node-12-99 — will report results in 10m.
alex: thanks. If latency returns, escalate to network oncall and prepare rolling reboot plan during maintenance window.
